- No git, and no GitHub account
- No OSF account – we read OSF as readers, without logging in
- No finished installation yet: Task 1 sets yours up, and the browser lab is there as a fallback

**Do this now:** open your workspace folder in your IDE, and open the browser lab in a tab beside it; R loads in the page while we talk.

::: notes
Before anything else, a word on what you do not need. You do not need git or a GitHub account, and you do not need an OSF account either, because we will look at the OSF from the outside, as readers do. If your installation is not finished yet, that is fine: the first hands-on task gets everybody set up properly, and the browser lab on the course site runs the same exercise inside a web page if your machine refuses. One thing to do right now, while I talk. Open the workspace folder in your IDE, then open the browser lab in a tab beside it and leave it alone. R loads there in the background, so it will be ready long before you might need it.
:::
